2026-10-27
Professor Hung-Chung Hsueh of Tamkang University's Department of Physics, along with alumnus and postdoctoral researcher Chih-En Hsu and an international research team, recently published two significant findings in the prestigious international journals Nature Chemistry and Physical Review Letters. Through international collaboration, the team not only stabilized an exotic quantum state at room temperature that previously existed only at extremely low temperatures, but also developed a new method for accurately calculating the properties of semiconductor materials. These breakthroughs lay an important foundation for the future development of electric vehicle chips and quantum computers. In the first study, Hsueh and Hsu collaborated with research teams from the Departments of Chemistry and Biochemistry and Materials Science and Engineering at the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA), the Department of Chemical Engineering and Materials Science at the University of Southern California (USC), and the University of Chemistry and Technology in the Czech Republic, among others. They published their findings in Nature Chemistry, a leading chemistry journal with a five-year impact factor of 24. Previously, exotic quantum phenomena in a two-dimensional layered quantum material known as "1T-TaS₂" could only be maintained at extremely low temperatures of approximately −93°C (180 K), significantly limiting its potential for practical applications. To overcome this temperature limitation, the research team adopted an innovative "molecular engineering" strategy, intercalating arginine molecules, an amino acid, between the material's atomic layers to create a "1T-TaS₂/arginine hybrid superlattice." This approach successfully raised the temperature at which the quantum state remains stable to above room temperature (330 K), providing a novel chemical pathway for controlling the quantum states of materials. In another study, Hsueh and Hsu collaborated with a research team led by Professor Zhenglu Li of USC, and they published their findings in Physical Review Letters, a highly regarded physics journal with a five-year impact factor of 9.3. In chips used in smartphones, computers, and electric vehicles, electron movement is affected by interactions with atomic vibrations within the material, directly influencing device operating speeds and power consumption. Existing computational simulation methods have limitations in accurately calculating these interactions. To address this issue, the research team used a more comprehensive theoretical approach that accounts for electron interactions. Their calculations revealed that conventional methods underestimate these interactions by approximately 15% in silicon carbide, a key material used in electric vehicles. This more accurate computational method not only helps researchers identify promising high-performance materials before experiments, reducing research and development costs, but also helps select materials that extend the stable operating time of future quantum computers. Hsueh explained that the exotic quantum phenomena exhibited by novel materials represent important fundamental research topics of shared interest in physics and chemistry. The Nature Chemistry paper brought together researchers from multiple international teams, demonstrating the highly interdisciplinary nature of materials research. The paper's subsequent citations and academic impact will also contribute to the research performance of relevant departments at Tamkang University, further strengthening the university's overall academic achievements. He added that both breakthroughs were built upon the Department of Physics' long-established expertise in theoretical and computational research. Hsueh expressed particular gratitude for Tamkang University's sustained support in providing research facilities and resources, while also recognizing Hsu's dedication to computational implementation. Looking ahead, the team plans to extend this computational methodology to a broader range of semiconductor and two-dimensional material systems, while continuing to collaborate with international partners to advance research on materials for electronic devices and quantum information technologies.
2026-10-27
Since assuming office on August 1, Tamkang University President Hui-Huang Hsu has identified four major challenges facing the university: a sharp decline in the student population and the resulting enrollment crisis, pressure to transform amid the AI revolution, the dual challenges of attracting and retaining talent, and changing learning patterns among the new generation of students. He has also formulated corresponding strategies to address these challenges and chart a new course for the university. Recently, he was invited to share these plans and initiatives at major academic events, including the International Higher Education Forum, themed "Reimagining Universities in the AI Era," held as part of Shih Hsin University's 70th anniversary celebrations, and the 2026 Taiwan–Germany Online Higher Education Forum. At the two forums, President Hsu delivered presentations titled "Reimagining Universities in the AI Era: From Imparting Knowledge to Cultivating Judgment" and "Beyond the Classroom: How AI Is Reshaping Teaching, Learning, and Governance at a Comprehensive University," respectively. He emphasized that in the AI era, when knowledge is readily accessible, the most essential and increasingly scarce capability universities must cultivate is sound judgment—the ability to ask the right questions, verify information accuracy, integrate knowledge across disciplines, and take responsibility for decisions. Tamkang University is reshaping its university ecosystem through redesigned teaching methods, smarter governance, and strategic internationalization. President Hsu noted that despite the severe challenges Taiwan's declining birthrate poses to higher education, Tamkang University continues to demonstrate strong institutional performance and brand appeal. The registration rate for its daytime undergraduate programs has exceeded 101% for three consecutive years, reaching 101.84% in the 2026–2027 academic year. The university also ranks first nationwide in the number of incoming first-year undergraduate students. To address future enrollment challenges, Tamkang University will continue strengthening partnerships with high schools, enhancing international student recruitment, and leveraging its extensive global network of more than 340,000 alumni to build a solid foundation for sustainable institutional development. President Hsu emphasized that AI has not undermined universities; rather, it has exposed the vulnerabilities of traditional educational systems. Drawing inspiration from Shih Hsin University's founding motto, "Cultivating Both Virtue and Intellect, Applying Both Mind and Hands," he extended its spirit to the contemporary concepts of "human–AI collaboration" and "the integration of technology and the humanities." He proposed a comprehensive redefinition of three fundamental roles within the university: ▌ Students (Learners): Students must evolve from traditional "recipients of knowledge" into "orchestrators of human–AI collaboration." Beyond developing AI literacy, they must cultivate critical thinking skills and the ability to integrate knowledge across disciplines and apply it in practice. ▌ Faculty (Educators): Faculty members must transition from "knowledge transmitters" at the lectern to "learning designers and coaches." This involves redesigning assessment mechanisms to place greater emphasis on students' reasoning, thought processes, and exploration rather than merely evaluating their final outputs. ▌ University Governance (Administrators): University administration must advance from traditional "process management" to "data-driven intelligent governance." By leveraging data, universities can establish early warning systems for students experiencing learning difficulties, improve administrative efficiency, and allocate resources more precisely, while maintaining rigorous standards of information security and ethical responsibility. President Hsu further shared that, beginning in the 2025–2026 academic year, Tamkang University has comprehensively promoted the integration of generative AI into its curriculum and incorporated statements on the ethical use of AI into course syllabi. Building on the establishment of its College of Artificial Innovative Intelligence and partnerships with industry leaders such as Microsoft, AMD, and NVIDIA, the university is leveraging AI and ESG as two core strategic pillars to help small and medium-sized enterprises achieve net-zero carbon emissions and digital transformation. In conclusion, President Hsu stressed that university transformation should be "grounded in pedagogy rather than merely driven by tools, guided by sustainability principles in governance, and focused on investing in talent as a top priority." Looking ahead, Tamkang University will continue to foster a high-quality learning environment that promotes collaboration between humans and AI, empowering students to become "active architects of their personalized learning journeys" and "guardians of sound value judgments." By working closely with higher education institutions, government agencies, and industry partners at home and abroad, Tamkang aims to open a new chapter of innovation and collaboration.
2026-10-19
Tamkang University's Department of Global Politics and Economics held an in-person instruction week for its In-service Master's Program in Digital Learning in Asia-Pacific and Latin American Studies in the mid-October 2026–2027 academic year. 12 distinguished international participants from seven Latin American countries, including diplomats, think tank scholars, and prominent political figures, gathered at the university. Through face-to-face exchanges and dialogue, the program aimed to strengthen Taiwan's strategic partnerships and academic collaboration with Latin America. This year's 12 students are distinguished professionals from the political, economic, media, and academic sectors of seven Latin American countries: Guatemala, Paraguay, Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Ecuador, and Mexico. On October 15, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Ming-Chi Chen hosted a special luncheon in their honor. In his remarks, he welcomed distinguished participants from diverse professional backgrounds across Latin America and thanked Tamkang University for its longstanding efforts to promote exchanges between Taiwan and the region. During the luncheon hosted by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA), Professor Lorena Yael Piedra Cobo of the Asia-Pacific Affairs Research Program at the College of Security and Defense, Ecuador's National Institute of Advanced Studies, delivered remarks on behalf of the incoming students. She thanked MOFA and Tamkang University for thoughtfully organizing the program's courses and study visits. She noted that the visit provided valuable opportunities to gain an in-depth understanding of Taiwan's history, technological innovation, education, healthcare, and democratic governance, while also encouraging reflection on the development challenges currently facing Latin American countries. She emphasized that all participants would make the most of this opportunity to deepen their understanding of Taiwan and share their experiences upon returning home. They also hoped to apply what they had gained to further strengthen cooperation and friendship between Taiwan and Latin America. The students participating in this year's in-person program have impressive professional backgrounds, representing influential figures from government, industry, and academia across Latin America. Among the participants were Atanasio Bogado González, a retired Colonel affiliated with the Paraguayan Embassy in Taiwan, and his spouse; Andrea Nathalia Ruiz Jordan, First Secretary at Paraguay's diplomatic mission in the United Arab Emirates; Mario Fabián Silva, Confidential Secretary to Paraguay's Vice Minister of Foreign Affairs; Jorge Garicoche Centurión, advisor to the Paraguayan Banking Association; Paula Macarena Carro Olmedo, General Manager of Paraguay's Chamber of Commerce and Services; and Pedro Ramón Puerta, founder of Argentina's Activar political party. Through this e-learning master's program, Tamkang University has successfully attracted influential individuals from Latin America to Taiwan to learn from its experiences. The initiative not only expands the reach and depth of Taiwan's people-to-people diplomacy but also showcases the country's soft power in regional studies and higher education. During the intensive seven-day program of in-person classes and visits, participants explored political and economic developments in the Asia-Pacific and Latin American regions. They also engaged in direct dialogue with representatives from Taiwan's government and academic communities through luncheon gatherings and other activities carefully arranged by MOFA and Tamkang University. After the program successfully concluded, participants departed for their home countries over the weekend. They will continue their studies through online distance learning and, upon completing all required coursework, their master's theses, and oral defenses, will be awarded master's degrees.
2026-10-16
Tamkang University's Center for Holistic Education recently hosted a grand High Table Dinner at the Student Activity Center. President Hui-Huang Hsu, Vice President for Academic Affairs and Director of the Center for Holistic Education Hung-Chung Hsueh, and Vice President for International Affairs and Dean of the College of International Affairs Cheng-Hao Pao. Department chairs and full-time faculty members from the Center's English-taught bachelor's programs in Computer Science and Information Engineering, Business Administration, English, International Tourism Management, and Global Politics and Economics joined first-year students, all dressed in formal attire. With 50 tables arranged for the occasion, nearly 300 faculty members and students gathered to celebrate this annual event. Originating from the collegiate traditions of the Universities of Oxford and Cambridge in the United Kingdom, the High Table Dinner has become an integral part of the Center for Holistic Education's freshman welcome traditions. All participants dressed formally, demonstrating their understanding of international etiquette and respect for the occasion. The event also gives students a chance to prepare for cross-cultural exchanges and international engagement through Tamkang University's "Study Abroad in the Junior Year" program. Dean of the College of Engineering Li-Chiu Chang, Dean of the College of Business and Management Chao-Che Hsu, Dean of the College of Foreign Languages and Literatures Ching-Gwo Chang, Dean of Student Affairs Yen-Ling Lin, and Dean of International Affairs Chien-Mu Yeh also joined the celebration, raising their glasses and enjoying conversations with students. In his remarks, President Hsu explained that the Center's holistic educational system encompasses three key features: all-English instruction, all-residential living, and all studying abroad during the junior year. At its core is the goal of developing students' international mobility. He encouraged the first-year students to make friends across departments and nationalities during their time at Tamkang University. He also praised the students for dressing formally, emphasizing that formal attire symbolizes the transition into adulthood. He expressed his hope that, beginning that evening, students would cultivate a mature mindset and take responsibility for their actions. Vice President Hsueh noted that although AI can assist with tasks and generate content in the AI era, it cannot replace face-to-face conversations, sincere listening, and the development of genuine trust and human connections. He encouraged everyone to put aside their mobile phones for a while and not worry about speaking perfect English. Instead, he urged them to approach one another with sincerity and understanding, using dinner-table conversations to foster meaningful, warm cross-cultural exchanges. National flags from around the world were displayed throughout the venue, highlighting its multicultural atmosphere. Before dinner began, a special dining etiquette session introduced participants to proper Western tableware and seating etiquette. Following the remarks, President Hsu led faculty members and students in raising their glasses and enthusiastically calling out "Cheers!" to officially open the dinner. Full-time faculty members from various departments sat alongside students, creating a lively and welcoming atmosphere for interaction and conversation. Assistant Professor I-Ya Chen of the Department of Business Administration, who attended the dinner, remarked, "It is wonderful to see everyone dressed so elegantly tonight!" She noted that first-year students are often shy when they first enter university, but sharing a meal at the same table helps break the ice and effectively brings faculty members and students closer together. She encouraged students to courageously explore their interests throughout their four years at university and embrace a more colorful and fulfilling college experience. Student representative Katherine Yong Shing Wei, a first-year student in the English-taught Business Administration program, said she chose a white dress to show respect for her professors and university administrators. Although she initially felt nervous sitting directly across from the college deans, their approachable manner and willingness to share their study-abroad experiences and information about Tamkang University's learning resources soon put her at ease. Fellow first-year Business Administration student Yu-Xuan Lin, who sat at the same table, said she rarely wears formal attire but had carefully dressed up for the dinner. The experience also gave her a profound sense of personal growth, as though she were participating in a coming-of-age ceremony.
2026-10-06
Two student teams from Tamkang University's Department of International Tourism Management recently achieved outstanding results at the 2026 Campus International Golden Travel Awards Tour Itinerary Design Competition, widely regarded as the "Oscars of the Travel Industry." Competing against 142 teams nationwide, the two teams emerged as national champions in the Domestic Tourism and Inbound Tourism categories, respectively, among 24 outstanding itineraries selected for recognition. After winning a national championship in one category during its debut participation last year, the department achieved an even greater milestone this year by sweeping both national titles, impressing participating travel industry professionals and representatives from related academic departments. The team behind "漫步東海岸，花現好時光" was also invited to attend the awards ceremony scheduled for December, where they will receive their award alongside winning teams from the travel industry. Assistant Professor Hsiu-Hui Chuang of the Department of International Tourism Management supervised both teams, and they entered the competition with their junior-year capstone projects. "人之島．海的記憶," entered in the Indigenous Communities subcategory of Domestic Tourism, and "漫步東海岸，花現好時光," entered in the Hong Kong and Macau Visitors to Taiwan subcategory of Inbound Tourism, each secured a national championship. Department Chair Shan-Ju Chi congratulated the award-winning students and their advisor, declaring, "You are the pride of our department!" She noted that sweeping both national championships in the Campus Golden Travel Awards was a testament to the students' solid professional expertise and teamwork. She also expressed special appreciation to Chuang for her dedicated professional guidance and unwavering support, which helped students bridge the gap between academic learning and professional excellence. Chuang recalled telling her students at the outset, "If I supervise your projects, I will be very demanding, and we will spend a great deal of time discussing and revising them repeatedly." She was delighted that the students were willing to accept the challenge despite knowing what lay ahead. Throughout the preparation process, the teams held countless meetings, conducted extensive research, and repeatedly refined their proposals. Every aspect of their itineraries, from transportation, accommodation, and dining to sightseeing arrangements, had to balance sustainable tourism principles with practical feasibility. What moved Chuang most was that the students never gave up, even though they knew that each revision might lead to further changes. Instead, they remained committed to improving their work through continuous adjustments. She believes that winning both national championships was the most rewarding recognition of the students' dedication and perseverance. The "人之島．海的記憶" team consisted of Department graduate Shu-Ting Kung and fourth-year students Wai Laam Chan, Yu-Ting Tsai, and Shan-Ju Lee. Centered on the culture of Orchid Island's (Lanyu) Tao Indigenous people, the team designed a four-day, three-night itinerary. The students explained that they chose Orchid Island because of its distinctive Indigenous culture, which differs from that of Taiwan's main island. They hoped visitors would do more than simply visit tourist attractions; instead, they wanted travelers to immerse themselves in local communities and gain firsthand insights into Tao culture through food, everyday life, and the natural environment. The itinerary incorporated local specialties featuring flying fish and visits to volcanic rock formations, connecting cultural experiences with natural landscapes. "We hope that by the end of the journey, travelers will have genuinely experienced an Indigenous culture distinct from that of Taiwan's main island and gained a deeper appreciation of Orchid Island's unique characteristics," the team explained. However, the greatest challenge in designing the itinerary was not selecting attractions but ensuring that the proposed tour could actually be carried out. Kung explained that the team had to verify every detail, from distances between attractions and transportation routes to whether accommodations and restaurants were legally registered. They also needed to confirm accessibility to certain mountainous attractions. As a result, the team revised its routes and continued refining the itinerary under their advisor's guidance to ensure that the proposal was more than just a plan on paper. The students agreed that this process gave them the most valuable learning experience. The other team, consisting of three close friends and Department graduates Jui-Chi Chen, Ting-Yu Chung, and Mandy Chen, designed a five-day tour of eastern Taiwan covering Yilan, Hualien, and Taitung under the theme "漫步東海岸，花現好時光." Targeting travelers aged 20 to 39 from Hong Kong and Macau, the itinerary featured hot-air balloon experiences, all-terrain vehicle rides, Indigenous cultural activities, and eastern Taiwan's natural landscapes. The team hoped to introduce visitors from Hong Kong and Macau to aspects of Taiwan that differ from what they commonly experience in the island’s western part. Although the itinerary originated as a capstone project, the students were determined to achieve the highest possible quality and revised their proposal repeatedly. They devoted considerable time to researching flight schedules, transportation options, accommodations, and dining arrangements. They also used Google Maps to verify driving times between attractions, minimize unnecessary backtracking, and ensure that the itinerary was realistically executable. When selecting accommodations, they considered not only prices, distances, and room types but also hotel star ratings and relevant operator information. The final-day itinerary underwent particularly significant revisions. The original plan involved traveling from Yilan through the Hsuehshan Tunnel to Taoyuan International Airport. However, concerned that heavy northbound weekend traffic could cause delays, the team revised the schedule to include a morning visit to Elephant Mountain in Taipei, followed by lunch at Zhuwei Fishing Harbor before heading to the airport. This adjustment was intended to reduce the risk of transportation delays. Organized by the Travel Quality Assurance Association, the Golden Travel Awards were originally established as a competition for travel industry professionals. To encourage emerging talent in tourism, the organizers introduced a student category in 2022, which has now entered its fifth year. In terms of academic-field classification, due to a decline in the number of humanities and social sciences departments, Tamkang was reclassified for the first time from the Humanities and Social Sciences category to the Comprehensive Universities (excluding Humanities and Social Sciences and Medicine) category, in which it ranked 18th nationwide. Tamkang also appeared in the peer assessments for three additional fields: Mass Communication, Languages, and Services, ranking 7th, 8th, and 8th nationwide, respectively. The university ranked 21st overall in competitiveness.

Professor Ben-Hang Chang, Director of the Carrie Chang Fine Arts Center and Professor in the Department of Chinese Literature at Tamkang University, was recently awarded the Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Rosette by the Government of Japan. An investiture ceremony was held at 11:30 a.m. on June 16 at the Okura Prestige Taipei Hotel, where Kazuyuki Katayama, Chief Representative of the Japan–Taiwan Exchange Association Taipei Office, presented the medal and certificate to Chang in recognition of his longstanding dedication to the art of calligraphy and his contributions to cultural exchanges between Taiwan and Japan. Among those attending the ceremony were Tamkang University President Huan-Chao Keh, Chairperson Flora Chia-I Chang, Director-General of the National Dr. Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall Lan-Sheng Wang, Kuo Hua Golf Chairman Liu-Lienlien Ho, soprano Susie Chien, and entertainers Bingbing Pai and Lie Yang. Former Premier Si-Kun You and former Democratic Progressive Party Secretary-General Kuo-Yung Hsu were invited to deliver congratulatory remarks. “Receiving this Japanese decoration is a great honor, but also the starting point for continued efforts,” Chang said during his speech. He noted that the award represents not only a significant personal milestone but also recognition of the long-term achievements of Taiwan–Japan calligraphy exchanges. He expressed gratitude to the Japan–Taiwan Exchange Association and supporters from various sectors, while reaffirming his commitment to further strengthening cultural cooperation between the two countries. Reflecting on his career, Chang recalled that his connection with Japan began during his student years through calligraphy exhibitions. He has since held 12 solo calligraphy exhibitions across Japan and hosted the television programs Chinese Calligraphy and One Character a Day for 25 years. During that period, he made numerous visits to Japan to document developments in Japanese calligraphy culture and welcomed Japanese calligraphy delegations to Taiwan, facilitating major joint exhibitions and academic exchange activities. At Tamkang University, with the support of Chairperson Chang and President Keh, Chang has led the development of the Intelligent e-Pen, an innovative digital calligraphy platform that integrates artificial intelligence into calligraphy education. The project has attracted considerable attention from Japan’s calligraphy community. In recent years, working with a research team led by Dean Tzung-Hang Lee and in collaboration with STUDIO A, the team has further combined e-Pen and AI technologies to develop intelligent systems featuring virtual brushwriting and automatic artwork layout functions. Several Japanese institutions offering specialized calligraphy programs have since visited Tamkang University for training and collaborative exchanges, while distance-learning initiatives have further strengthened partnerships. Chang and his team are currently developing a Japanese-language version of the Intelligent e-Pen Calligraphy Learning System, aiming to create a new model for preserving and promoting traditional culture. In addition to receiving a congratulatory message from President Ching-te Lai, Chang also received congratulatory telegrams from former President of Japan’s House of Councilors Akiko Santo, Chairman of the Japan–ROC Diet Members’ Consultative Council Keiji Furuya, and Taiwan’s Representative to Japan I-Yang Lee. In a congratulatory message, Tsuyoshi Kinoshita, Director of the Office of Sanae Takaichi, praised Chang’s longstanding contributions to Taiwan–Japan cultural exchanges. Former Japanese Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba also commended Chang’s efforts in promoting Taiwan–Japan calligraphy exchanges and nurturing talent through his leadership roles as President of the International Calligraphy Alliance and the Calligraphy Society of the Republic of China. Ishiba further highlighted Chang’s digital innovations, including the Intelligent e-Pen, which have helped preserve traditional culture and serve as an important bridge for deepening mutual understanding between Taiwan and Japan.

To introduce international students to Taiwan's traditional festivals and cultural heritage, the International Student Guidance Section of Tamkang University's Office of International and Cross-Strait Affairs hosted the "Dragon Boat Festival Rice Dumpling Celebration" at noon on June 10 in the lobby on the 10th floor of the Ching-Sheng Memorial Building. The event welcomed international students from around the world to celebrate the Dragon Boat Festival together. Vice President for International Affairs Hsiao-Chuan Chen and Dean of International Affairs Chien-Mu Yeh also joined the celebration, sharing the festive atmosphere with students. The event began with an English presentation by Shiena Chailand, a senior student in the English-taught Computer Science and Information Engineering Program from Indonesia, who introduced the origins of the Dragon Boat Festival. She recounted the story of the patriotic poet Qu Yuan and explained the historical significance of dragon boat racing and rice dumplings (zongzi), emphasizing that the festival not only represents an important traditional celebration but also embodies the cultural values of integrity, loyalty, and selfless devotion. Her engaging presentation helped many international students gain a deeper appreciation of a festival they were experiencing for the first time. Following the cultural presentation, faculty members and students gathered for a group photo before receiving traditional rice dumplings. Many students eagerly sampled this iconic Taiwanese delicacy while chatting with friends from different countries and exchanging stories about their own cultural traditions. Plates and chili sauce were thoughtfully provided, allowing participants to enjoy the rice dumplings according to their personal tastes. Angel Felicia, a senior student in the Department of Business Administration from Indonesia, shared that she is currently working in Taipei and therefore has fewer opportunities to meet with classmates. She appreciated the event not only for allowing her to enjoy a traditional Dragon Boat Festival delicacy but also for providing a chance to reconnect with friends and experience the warmth of campus celebrations. Jessica Chen, a first-year student in the Department of International Business from France, said she had learned about the Dragon Boat Festival while studying Chinese in France, but this was the first time she had gained a deeper understanding of its historical background and tasted zongzi. She remarked that the event not only introduced her to Taiwanese culture but also gave her the opportunity to make new friends. Emma Majek, a first-year student in the French Section of the Department of European Languages from France, noted that France also has festive traditions associated with special foods. During Epiphany (Épiphanie), families enjoy Galette des Rois (King Cake), while La Chandeleur (Candlemas) is celebrated by eating crêpes. She commented that discovering cultures through food is both enjoyable and meaningful and expressed her hope of watching a Dragon Boat Festival race in Taiwan in the future. Su Thi Phuong Lo`an, a first-year student in the Department of Information and Communication from Vietnam, shared that the Dragon Boat Festival in Vietnam is also known as the "Insect-Killing Festival." On that day, families traditionally gather early in the morning to eat fermented glutinous rice and sour fruits, believing these foods promote good health and drive away illness. Although the Dragon Boat Festival is celebrated differently in Taiwan and Vietnam, she observed that both traditions emphasize family reunions and the preservation of cultural heritage.

The Center for European Union Studies at Tamkang University, together with the University Social Responsibility (USR) project "From Tamsui to the World: Promoting Taiwan's Most Influential Cultural Tours and Signature Banquets" (hereafter the Tour & Banquet Project), hosted the "Hobe European Cultural Feast" on June 12. The event welcomed representatives, commercial officers, and scholars from the European Economic and Trade Office (EETO) and more than ten European countries, including the Czech Republic, France, Belgium, Poland, and the Netherlands. Guests gathered at the Fullon Hotel Tamsui Fisherman's Wharf to experience the "Hobe Banquet 1002 – French Naval Bombardment," a themed dining experience jointly developed by the USR project team and the Fullon Hotel. Through an innovative culinary interpretation of history, the event created a unique platform for cultural and academic diplomacy. Tamkang University has long been committed to European studies. In addition to its Graduate Institute of European Studies and Department of European Languages and Cultures, the University is home to one of the few European Union Centers and EU Information Centers in a university library in Taiwan. It also maintains close and longstanding academic partnerships with European representative offices in Taiwan. Professor Li-Jiuan Chen, Director of the Center for EU Studies and the organizer of the event, explained that, as one of Taiwan's leading academic institutions for EU studies, the University hoped to help European diplomats better understand the historical significance of the Battle of Hobe and its lasting influence on Taiwan through both the Hobe Banquet and a cultural cruise along the Tamsui River, while also showcasing Taiwan's rich cultural heritage. At noon, the delegation enjoyed the "Hobe Banquet 1002 – French Naval Bombardment" in the Fullon Hotel Tamsui. The banquet was personally introduced by Professor Chi-Lin Lee, Chair of the Department of History and Principal Investigator of the USR Tour & Banquet Project, who explained the historical significance behind each dish. Featuring ten creatively designed courses—including Four-Warship Salvo, symbolizing the French naval assault, and Rain of Fire, representing the bombardment—the menu vividly recreated the events of the Battle of Tamsui during the Sino-French War in October 1884. Tamkang University's Academic Vice President Hui-Huang Hsu, Dean of Research and Development Po-Shen Pan, Dean of the College of Foreign Languages and Literatures Yi-Di Lin, and Professor Li-Jiuan Chen also served as table hosts, warmly welcoming the international guests. The event brought together an impressive gathering of distinguished guests, including Mr. Lukáš Gajdoš, Deputy Head of the European Economic and Trade Office; Mr. David Steinke, Representative of the Czech Economic and Cultural Office; Mr. Alexandre Kaufhold, Representative of the Luxembourg Trade and Investment Office, Taipei; Mr. Matthieu Branders, Representative of the Belgian Office, Taipei, and his wife; Mr. Janusz Bilski, Representative of the Polish Office in Taipei, and his wife; and Mr. Bastiaan Pulles, Representative of the Netherlands Office Taipei. Officials from Hungary, France, Finland, Sweden, the Spanish Chamber of Commerce, the European Chamber of Commerce Taiwan (ECCT), and the American Institute in Taiwan (AIT) also attended, joining interdisciplinary faculty members and Tamkang University's UAV research team for academic exchanges. Following the banquet, the delegation embarked on a cultural cruise along the Tamsui River, visiting the historic sites of the Battle of Tamsui. The journey served as a vivid demonstration of how local history, cultural creativity, and sustainable regional development can be integrated to promote international understanding and academic collaboration. Before attending the luncheon, Mr. Lukáš Gajdoš visited the University's EU Information Center in the Chueh-Sheng Memorial Library. He then delivered a keynote lecture entitled "The European Union and Taiwan," introducing current developments within the European Union to students from the Graduate Institute of European Studies, the Departments of Diplomacy and International Relations, History, Computer Science and Information Engineering, Public Administration, and European Languages. During the lively discussion session, students raised questions on topics including cross-strait security, EU enlargement, and nuclear energy. Gajdoš explained that the European Union primarily serves as a "soft-power partner" while remaining "firmly committed to its principles." Responding to questions about study and internship opportunities in Europe, he encouraged students to attend the annual European Education Fair in November, explore internationally oriented Erasmus Mundus programs, and apply for the one or two internship positions offered each year by the European Economic and Trade Office through its official website.

To support international students in pursuing careers in Taiwan and facilitate their transition into the workforce, Tamkang University's Office of International and Cross-Strait Affairs hosted the 2026 International Student Career Fair at 12:10 p.m. on May 29 in the Black Swan Exhibition Hall. The event brought together 12 companies to recruit talent, offering a wide range of employment opportunities and career information to help students better understand industry trends and prepare for their future careers. Participating companies included Da Da Broadband, Formosa Laboratories, McDonald's Taiwan, Sunny Pharmtech, Yuimom Constructing Taipei Branch, Kaori Heat Treatment, TaskUs Holdings Taiwan, Superrite Electronics, Ming Jing Beauty, Hi-Lai Foods, Galaxy Software Services, and Panasonic Taiwan. Company representatives introduced their organizations, outlined current recruitment needs, and later met face-to-face with students to discuss job openings, qualification requirements, and career prospects. The opening ceremony was officiated by Vice President for International Affairs Hsiao-Chuan Chen, who welcomed both corporate representatives and international students. She noted that, with a history spanning more than 75 years, Tamkang University has consistently produced graduates who are highly valued by employers and reaffirmed the University's commitment to providing comprehensive career guidance and employment support. The participating companies also shared insights into emerging industry trends. Galaxy Software highlighted its demand for Thai-speaking professionals, TaskUs Holdings Taiwan introduced its multilingual and multicultural international working environment, Sunny Pharmtech showcased its diverse global research and development team, while Kaori Heat Treatment presented career opportunities in AI server thermal management—one of today's fastest-growing technology sectors. These presentations helped students gain first-hand knowledge of current labor market demands. For international students, the fair was more than a recruitment event—it was an opportunity better to understand employer expectations and career development in Taiwan. Pannavit Soonthorn, a first-year master's student in Computer Science and Information Engineering from Thailand, said that although graduation is still some time away, he wanted to begin planning his future career early and therefore brought his résumé to the event. Interested in AI and information technology, he actively visited the booths of Da Da Broadband and Panasonic Taiwan. He commented that speaking directly with company representatives provided much deeper insights into the skills and qualifications employers truly value than simply browsing online job portals. Reflecting on the challenges faced by international students seeking employment in Taiwan, he noted that Chinese language proficiency remains one of the biggest barriers. "Improving my Chinese communication skills will definitely give me a greater advantage in the workplace," he said. He also hopes to strengthen his competitiveness by building a strong project portfolio. Hsin-Wei Peng, a sophomore student in the Department of Diplomacy and International Relations from the United States, said the event gave her valuable inspiration. She spoke with several companies and submitted her résumé, describing the experience as rewarding despite the challenge of conducting professional conversations in Chinese. After learning about her background, Formosa Laboratories invited her to apply for a summer internship. She admitted that she had originally planned to return to the United States after graduation, but the interactions with Taiwanese employers prompted her to reconsider staying in Taiwan to gain professional experience before deciding on her long-term career path. "I had never really interacted with Taiwanese companies before. After today's conversations, I realized there are actually many opportunities that are well-suited to international students," she said. The career fair also attracted many underclassmen eager to learn about Taiwan's employment market. Bryant Emmanuel Waslan, an Indonesian student enrolled in the International Foundation Program who plans to continue his studies in the Department of Computer Science and Information Engineering, said that although he is not yet looking for a job, he wanted to understand employers' expectations as early as possible. He shared that listening comprehension in Chinese remained his biggest challenge during conversations with recruiters, but the experience helped him identify the areas in which he needs to improve as he prepares for his future career.

As many junior students prepare for overseas exchange programs and international internships, they often encounter ambiguous workplace boundaries and cultural differences when entering multinational companies, translation agencies, or educational settings. To enhance gender equality awareness and promote a safer learning and internship environment, the College of Foreign Languages and Literatures at Tamkang University held a gender equality seminar on June 2 in FL106. The seminar was presented by Assistant Professor Wei-Ting Wang of the Department of English, who shared insights on gender boundaries in cross-cultural interactions, workplace self-protection, and teachers' responsibilities in reporting incidents of sexual harassment. Wang noted that students working under foreign supervisors or in overseas environments may mistakenly interpret inappropriate behavior as merely a "cultural difference." She emphasized that "cultural differences are never an excuse for inappropriate conduct." Any behavior that violates an individual's wishes or causes discomfort should be recognized as crossing personal boundaries. Drawing on real cases from internship settings, she illustrated how unequal power relationships can make students reluctant to speak up for fear of affecting their grades or performance evaluations. She encouraged students to document incidents by preserving messages, emails, or recordings whenever appropriate, and to seek assistance from their department or the University as early as possible. Addressing sexual harassment, Wang advised students to communicate their boundaries clearly and respectfully. Practical strategies include responding with clarifying questions, creating physical distance, and expressing discomfort in a calm but firm manner. She also reminded faculty members that when students seek help, they should avoid excessive questioning about the details of an incident and, in accordance with legal requirements, complete the mandatory report within 24 hours to ensure timely support and protection. In her concluding remarks, Wang stressed that every student has the right to bodily autonomy and personal dignity, whether studying or working in Taiwan or abroad. Students facing emergencies may contact Tamkang University's 24-hour Campus Security Center hotline (+886-2-2621-5656, ext. 2119 or 2110). Those requiring emotional or psychological support are encouraged to reach out to the Counseling, Career Development, and Learning Center (ext. 2221), where professional assistance and resources are readily available. Jia-Chi Lee, a junior student in the Department of Japanese, who will soon begin an internship at an overseas hotel, said the seminar reinforced an important message: "If I don't like it, I don't like it." She added that the session gave her greater confidence to express her feelings and establish clear personal boundaries whenever she encounters situations that make her uncomfortable.

Tamkang University held its 2026 Commencement Ceremony at 10:00 a.m. on June 6 on the 7th floor of the Shao-mo Memorial Gymnasium. More than 3,300 graduates, faculty members, parents, and distinguished guests from various colleges, departments, and graduate institutes gathered to celebrate the occasion. The ceremony opened with dynamic performances by the Competitive Cheerleading Team and the Dance Club. This year’s theme, “AI+SDGs=∞, ESG+AI=∞, A Favorite Among Employers,” symbolized the Tamkang spirit of harnessing intelligence and sustainability to create limitless opportunities for the future. The ceremony was presided over by President Huan-Chao Keh. Remarks were delivered by Chairperson Flora Chia-I Chang, Golden Eagle alumnus of the Department of Mechanical Engineering and Chairman of Innodisk Corporation, Chuan-Sheng Chien, and President of the Tamkang University Alumni Association Headquarters, Tzu-Hua Chuang. Distinguished guests included Chin-Tsai Chen, President of the Tamkang University Worldwide Alumni Association; Chih-Jen Su, President of the Tamkang University Alumni Association Headquarters of Departments; and international guests from Paraguay, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, and other countries. In his address, President Keh noted that Tamkang University has long maintained close ties with industry and has consistently stayed ahead of emerging trends. The University actively cultivates students’ interdisciplinary competencies in artificial intelligence and sustainability, preparing them to become AI-enabled green-collar professionals highly sought after in the future workforce. He highlighted that Tamkang has been ranked the No. 1 private university most favored by employers in Taiwan by CommonWealth Magazine Group for 29 consecutive years. Encouraging graduates to embrace the spirit of “AI+SDGs=∞” and “ESG+AI=∞,” he urged them to develop three essential future-oriented capabilities: solid professional expertise, interdisciplinary versatility, and diverse soft skills. Quoting NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang, “You will not lose your job to AI, but you may lose your competitiveness to someone who knows how to use AI better than you do,” President Keh emphasized that storytelling, creativity, and judgment are becoming even more valuable in the AI era. He concluded by wishing all graduates success and prosperity in their future endeavors. Chairperson Chang emphasized the University’s long-standing commitment to its Triple Objectives of Globalization, Information-oriented Education, and Future-oriented Education, while promoting balanced growth in the five Educational Disciplines of Conduct, Intelligence, Physical Education, Teamwork, and Beauty and fostering eight essential qualities. She noted that while AI is important, expertise in one’s professional field remains the foundation for success in society. As the only university in Taiwan that requires participation in student clubs as part of its curriculum, Tamkang provides students with valuable extracurricular experiences and skills that become distinctive competitive advantages in the workplace. Quoting former U.S. President Abraham Lincoln, “The best way to predict the future is to create it,” she encouraged graduates to regard commencement not as an ending but as the beginning of a new dream, to maintain a passion for lifelong learning, and to stay connected with their alma mater so that the Tamkang spirit may continue to thrive. Echoing Chairperson Chang’s remarks, Chien highlighted student clubs as one of Tamkang’s greatest strengths. Recalling his four years performing with a band in the Guitar Club, he shared many cherished memories. He remarked that the University not only provided professional knowledge but also shaped his worldview and laid the foundation for his career in the technology industry and his leadership of a globally recognized AI enterprise. Chien reminded graduates that the world is experiencing an unprecedented wave of AI innovation, yet no technology can replace human creativity, vision, and passion. He concluded with an inspiring message: “For the AI generation, how do you create your future self from your past self? The answer is that only your future self can create your future—and our future.” He encouraged graduates to boldly envision the most outstanding future they could be proud of and to pursue it with courage and determination. Chuang emphasized that Tamkang University possesses one of the largest and most united alumni networks in Taiwan. He warmly welcomed graduates into the alumni family and reminded them that no matter how high they fly or how far they go, alumni from every profession will remain their strongest supporters. Beyond standing alongside them on the paths of AI and sustainability, alumni will continue to provide opportunities and assistance. He encouraged graduates to “lead innovation through technology and define success through sustainability,” to remain curious and eager to learn amid change, to embrace the opportunities created by AI, and to uphold ESG values through kindness and integrity. During the ceremony, Academic Achievement Awards, Conduct Awards, Service Awards, Athletic Awards, and diplomas were presented. Graduate representative Yun-Yun Chien from the Department of International Business delivered a humorous and heartfelt speech that resonated with the audience. She recalled shared experiences such as staying up late to complete final projects and navigating the campus through wind and rain near the iconic “Tamkang Waterfall.” Speaking about AI, she jokingly described it as a form of “technology-enabled collaboration” and referred to her classmates as “survivors” who persevered through the pandemic and numerous challenges. She encouraged everyone to face the future with the courage to think outside the box and expressed hope that they would meet again someday in their future journeys. The ceremony concluded with a moving performance of To Youth by Ariel Tsai, led by the University Choir and several international students. Amid the sounds of confetti cannons, colorful streamers, and balloons filling the air, graduates exchanged heartfelt farewells with faculty members and one another, bringing the celebration to a memorable and successful close.

The Office of International and Cross-Strait Affairs of Tamkang University held the 2026 International Student Graduation Ceremony at 10:00 a.m. on June 4 in the Chang Yeo Lan International Conference Hall of the Hsu Shou-Chlien International Conference Center. Vice President for International Affairs Hsiao-Chuan Chen, Dean of International Affairs Chien-Mu Yeh, faculty members from various colleges and departments, and more than 200 family members attended the event to celebrate the achievements of 146 international graduates from around the world as they completed their studies and embarked on a new chapter in life. The ceremony not only marked the culmination of their academic journeys but also symbolized their readiness to step onto a broader international stage with the courage and knowledge they gained in Taiwan. In her remarks, Vice President Chen emphasized that while graduation signifies an ending, it is, in essence, a new beginning. She reflected on the challenges international students faced when they first arrived in Taiwan, including language barriers and cultural adjustment. Through perseverance and determination, however, they overcame both academic and personal obstacles, making Taiwan and Tamkang University an integral part of their life stories. She reminded graduates that although they would soon leave campus, Tamkang University would always remain their home in Taiwan. With more than 330,000 alumni and 151 alumni associations worldwide, the University's extensive alumni network would continue to serve as a strong source of support. She encouraged graduates to apply what they had learned to contribute to society and the world and to become future leaders and innovators. The ceremony continued with the presentation of Student Club Leadership Awards, Outstanding Service Awards, and diplomas. Faculty members took turns presenting awards, conferring degrees, and conducting the tassel-turning ceremony. Two overseas compatriot students from Indonesia delivered remarks as representatives of the graduating class. Shiena Chailand from the Department of Computer Science and Information Engineering and Cathleen Fiona Mallian from the Department of Business Administration shared how they had arrived in Taiwan with a mixture of uncertainty and curiosity and initially felt lost in a new environment. However, through participation in international exchange programs and student organizations, they developed independence, adaptability, and a strong sense of belonging. Quoting former British Prime Minister Winston Churchill, they encouraged their fellow graduates with the words: “Success is not final, failure is not fatal: it is the courage to continue that counts.” They expressed hope that wherever life may take them, they would continue to create positive change in the world. Representing international students, Jean-Francois Morin from Canada, from the graduating class of the Department of Banking and Finance, opened his speech with humor, noting that he was often mistaken for a professor. He recalled arriving at Tamkang during the COVID-19 pandemic, when students were required to quarantine in designated hotels upon entering Taiwan. He described the experience as a test of commitment and perseverance. Looking back on his four years at Tamkang, he said the experience had fostered empathy that transcended national boundaries and taught him how to face uncertainty through collaboration. Family members and friends traveled from near and far to attend the ceremony, many dressed in traditional attire from their home countries, adding vibrant multicultural colors to the event. The ceremony concluded with a commemorative video presentation, bringing this meaningful chapter of academic life to a heartfelt and memorable close. Hananta Suryajaya from Indonesia, a graduating student of the Department of International Business, shared the story behind his decision to study in Taiwan. With a smile, he explained that the opportunity originated from his father’s “strict requirement.” Having studied in Taiwan himself during his university years, Hananta Suryajaya’s father insisted that each of his children pursue higher education abroad to broaden their horizons, while limiting their choices to Asia for cultural reasons. He noted that Taiwan has long been a popular destination among Indonesian students. The warm support of fellow Indonesians and Taiwan’s welcoming environment made his overseas study experience far less lonely and filled it with many happy memories.

title: Overseas Students Orientation, Cheng-Hao Pao Encourages Students to Explore Taiwan with Courage 淡江大小事

text:
Date 2026-09-09 440 Clicks
To help international students adapt to campus life, the Office of International and Cross-Strait Affairs held the “Overseas Students Orientation for Academic Year 2026–2027” at 9:30 a.m. on September 9 in the Chang Yeo-Lan International Conference Hall at the Hsu Shou-Chlien International Conference Center. More than 360 new Tamkang students from around the world gathered for the event, creating a warm and lively atmosphere.
In his remarks, Vice President for International Affairs Cheng-Hao Pao drew on his own experience studying in the United Kingdom. With humor, he recalled arriving with a computer and a Tatung rice cooker, and the anxiety he felt while searching for his dormitory on an almost deserted campus. His story resonated deeply with students facing the uncertainty of arriving in an unfamiliar environment. “When you encounter difficulties, don’t immediately think about giving up, and don’t feel that you are alone, because you still have us,” he said. He emphasized that Tamkang University and the Office of International and Cross-Strait Affairs would always stand behind the students. He encouraged new international students to build student associations, support one another, step outside their comfort zones, explore Taiwan with curiosity, and make every effort to learn Chinese. By combining Chinese proficiency with their existing language skills, he noted, students could create even more possibilities for their future and turn their study-abroad experience into an unforgettable journey.
The event also featured a series of briefings on campus life. Yi-Jie Dong, an officer from the Tamsui Precinct of the New Taipei City Police Department, emphasized the principle that “prevention is better than cure,” sharing personal safety tips and a three-step approach to fraud prevention. She also reminded students to remember the “165” anti-fraud hotline and the “110” police emergency number. Counseling psychologist Hao-Ju Hsu used lively scenario-based exercises to discuss cross-cultural communication and interpersonal boundaries, emphasizing that mutual respect for one another’s feelings is an essential foundation for cultural adaptation and gender equality. Hsing-Yu Lin, a staff member of the Department of English, explained the regulations governing English courses and reminded eligible students to apply for English course waivers within the first two weeks of the semester and to take other elective courses to make up the required graduation credits. The briefing was designed to help international students plan their academic paths with confidence.
Toward the end of the event, Dean of International Affairs Chien-Mu Yeh encouraged students to “study seriously, enjoy life fully, and put your plans into action,” urging them to balance academic work with exploring life beyond the classroom. He then introduced the international affairs team one by one and explained the various support services available to students. He also introduced a variety of student organizations, including associations for international, Indonesian, Japanese, and Vietnamese students, helping newcomers become familiar with the campus more quickly and begin their new chapter at Tamkang with confidence.
The new students also shared their hopes and expectations for university life. Isa Shimoyama, a first-year student in the Department of Chinese from Japan, said that because her mother is Taiwanese, she decided to study in Taiwan to strengthen her Chinese proficiency and hopes to make more local friends. Azael Emmanuel Cobb, a first-year student in the Department of International Business from Russia, said that various university offices provided detailed explanations that helped him quickly understand where to seek assistance on campus. He plans to focus fully on his studies while actively immersing himself in Taiwanese culture. Ai-Ling Cheng, a first-year student in the Department of Diplomacy and International Relations from Indonesia, expressed appreciation for the warm welcome from faculty members and fellow students, and said she looks forward to expanding her international social circle while taking on the challenge of learning a new language.

title: From Student Clubs to AI + SDGs, Tamkang University’s New Student and Parent Forum Highlights Key Issues for University Life 淡江大小事
heading: Date 2026-09-05 462 Clicks
text:
Date 2026-09-05 462 Clicks
The Office of Student Affairs held the “2026–2027 New Student and Parent Forum” at 10:00 a.m. on September 5 on the seventh floor of the Shao-mo Memorial Gymnasium. President Hui-Huang Hsu, joined by the university’s three vice presidents, college deans, and relevant first- and second-level administrators, met face-to-face with nearly 1,000 students and parents. The forum covered a wide range of topics, including student clubs, academic programs, overseas exchange opportunities, AI, and sustainability education, helping new students become familiar with the campus and plan their university experience.
In his remarks, President Hsu noted that since its founding in 1950, Tamkang University has upheld an open liberal academic tradition together with a strong commitment to education. The university has achieved success in institutional performance and international rankings. Despite Taiwan’s declining birth rate, Tamkang maintains an enrollment of nearly 22,000 students. He highlighted two distinctive features of the university: the “Triple Objectives of Internationalization, Information-Oriented Education, and Future-Oriented Education,” which Tamkang has promoted since 1965, and its unique mandatory student club participation program. In the age of artificial intelligence, he emphasized that interpersonal communication and teamwork are more important than ever, and the university hopes to develop these essential soft skills through student club participation.
In response to the rapid development of AI, President Hsu said Tamkang has established the College of Artificial Innovative Intelligence and the Department of Artificial Intelligence, while also collaborating with major international technology companies such as Microsoft Taiwan, NVIDIA, and AMD. All first-year students are required to take “Introduction to Artificial Intelligence.” In recent years, thousands of students from non-information technology fields have earned internationally recognized AI professional certifications from organizations such as Microsoft and NVIDIA, demonstrating strong outcomes in interdisciplinary learning. Tamkang University also plans to establish an “AI Governance Committee” as soon as possible to ensure that the development and use of AI comply with standards of safety, regulatory compliance, and ethics, while cultivating students’ abilities in self-directed learning, critical thinking, and interdisciplinary application.
During the discussion session, new students and parents asked about student clubs, academic programs, and overseas exchange opportunities, with relevant administrators responding to each topic. Dean of Student Affairs Yen-Ling Lin explained that Tamkang University currently has 184 active student clubs and encouraged students to build their interpersonal networks and teamwork experience through club participation. Te-Cheng Cheng, Head of the Extracurricular Activities Guidance Section, added that student clubs span eight major categories, including academic, athletic, and recreational organizations. The “Student Club Expo” was held on September 10 and 11, during the first week of classes, followed by “Club Night” on September 14, helping new students find organizations that match their interests.
Regarding junior-year study abroad and exchange opportunities, Dean of International Affairs Chien-Mu Yeh explained that, apart from five departments under the university’s “Holistic Education” model in which overseas study during the junior year is mandatory, all Tamkang students are eligible to apply for approximately 360 exchange places offered each year. He encouraged students interested in studying abroad to maintain strong academic performance and prepare early to meet the relevant qualifications.
Dean of Academic Affairs Li-Ren Yang introduced Tamkang University’s interdisciplinary learning system. Double majors and traditional minors require additional credits beyond the standard graduation requirements and therefore involve a relatively high threshold. Students may instead make use of the university’s “embedded-credit” second major and minor options. Within the existing 128 credits required for graduation, students can complete 40 credits in another field to earn a second specialization, or 20 credits to complete a minor. He also encouraged students to enroll in interdisciplinary certificate programs, while advising them not to choose fields too similar to their original major. He said that by venturing into different disciplines, students can strengthen their future competitiveness in the workplace.
In response to a parent’s question about how Tamkang University helps students internalize the concepts of “AI+SDGs=∞” and “ESG+AI=∞” as part of their everyday mindset, President Hsu explained that the required first-year courses “Introduction to Artificial Intelligence” and “Exploring Sustainability” provide students with foundational knowledge. The university also encourages each academic department to integrate AI and sustainability topics into its curriculum. In addition, through the “Campus Living Lab” competition, students are encouraged to form teams, identify sustainability issues on campus, propose solutions, and put those into practice. Vice President for Administrative Affairs Huei-Chun Chi added that the College of Liberal Arts offers the “Smart Humanities Practice and Innovation Credit Program,” which uses real-world settings such as regional revitalization and University Social Responsibility (USR) projects to guide students in exploring the possibilities created by integrating AI and sustainability.
Following the forum, new students and parents continued discussions with their departments. Department chairs introduced curriculum features, professional development opportunities, and future career pathways. The parent of a first-year student in the Department of Business Administration praised the forum, noting that it addressed concerns about future overseas study opportunities and also provided satisfying information about academic programs and student clubs. The parent said the session also showed that students could seek assistance if they encounter difficulties, giving the family greater confidence about the student’s university life.
The parent of a first-year student in the Department of Chemistry shared that the student already had a strong interest in chemistry and was very satisfied after hearing the department introduction and curriculum briefing. title: Tamkang University’s Achievements in Futures Studies Gain Global Recognition Again as Kuo-Hua Chen Receives APFN Individual Contribution Award 淡江大小事
heading: Date 2026-09-14 490 Clicks
text:
Date 2026-09-14 490 Clicks
Tamkang University’s achievements in advancing futures studies continue to attract international attention. Following the presentation of an individual award to Tamkang University Chairperson Flora Chia-I Chang last year, the 12th Asia Pacific Futures Network Conference (APFN12) this year presented the “APFN Award 2026” in the category of “Individual Contributions in an Institution Enhancing Futures Thinking in the Asia-Pacific Community” to Kuo-Hua Chen, Dean of the College of Education at Tamkang University. The award recognizes his long-standing efforts to promote futures thinking education, integrate foresight into the university’s overall curriculum, and contribute to the development of the futures studies community across the Asia-Pacific region.
This year’s conference was held on September 3 and 4 at the Sasin School of Management, Chulalongkorn University, in Bangkok, Thailand. Under the theme “Asia Pacific Futures—Powering People, Planet, Prosperity, and Peace,” the event brought together futures researchers, practitioners, policymakers, academics, and business leaders to explore future challenges related to people, the planet, prosperity, and peace. More than 244 participants from 40 countries attended. According to APFN, Chen has not only remained deeply engaged in academic research and educational practice related to futures thinking, but has also played a key role in Tamkang University’s development as an important global hub for foresight education.
One of the major sessions at this year’s conference was the special dialogue “Asia Pacific Futures—Advancing People, Planet, Prosperity, and Peace,” featuring Sohail Inayatullah, Visiting Researcher in Tamkang University’s Department of Education and Futures Design, and internationally renowned strategic futurist Professor Richard Hames. Inayatullah, the inaugural UNESCO Chair in Futures Studies, is ranked among the world’s top 2% most-cited scientists and originator of influential futures methodologies such as Causal Layered Analysis (CLA) and the Futures Triangle. He has long been dedicated to futures teaching, research, and curriculum development at Tamkang University. Richard Hames is a strategic futurist, author, and senior adviser whose work focuses on deep systemic change, organizational strategy, and civilizational transformation. Their dialogue centered on how societies can move beyond merely reacting to global change and instead actively shape a peaceful, prosperous, and sustainable future for the Asia-Pacific region. They also explored the role of regional foresight in responding to complex systems and high levels of uncertainty. The session further highlighted Tamkang University’s strong ties with the international futures studies community.
The Tamkang University delegation from the College of Education included three faculty members who served in different capacities as session chairs, facilitators, and research presenters. Dean Kuo-Hua Chen chaired the academic session “Tamkang University PhD Students Research Presentations,” guiding doctoral students as they shared their latest research and exchanged views with international scholars.
Associate Professor Nur Anisah Binti Abdullah of the Department of Education and Futures Design co-facilitated the workshop “Feminist Futures Mosaic: From Seeds to Possibilities” with international futures scholars. Using a simplified form of CLA, the workshop guided participants to begin with personal experiences and micro-narratives and explore issues involving care, power, voice, knowledge, justice, and transformation.
Assistant Professor Chun-Ta Chiu of the Department of Education and Futures Design presented “Curating Public Futures: Local Knowledge, Cultural Sustainability, and Anticipatory Governance—a Case of the Futures City Museum Project” in the academic track on futures-oriented research in the Asia-Pacific region. From the perspectives of curatorial practice and local engagement, he explained how local knowledge, cultural sustainability, and anticipatory governance can be brought together to create spaces in which society can collectively imagine public futures.
Six doctoral students from the Department of Education and Futures Design also represented Tamkang at the conference: Ricardo Schnug, Edward Niedbalski, Po-Ta Chen, An-Ting Kuo, Fang-Chun Liao, and Pohung Tseng. They presented their work in the “Academic Track: Tamkang University PhD Students Research Presentations,” which showcased the latest research by doctoral students and emerging scholars. Topics ranged from declining global school enrollment and weak signals in education, extreme weather and labor protection, open-source collaboration and paperless futures, the deconstruction and reconstruction of work through human-AI collaboration, to family narratives and subjectivity. Together, the presentations demonstrated the diverse ways in which Tamkang doctoral students apply futures theories and methods to issues in education, technology, the environment, and society.
Kuo-Hua Chen said that by having faculty members take part in academic moderation, participatory workshops, and research presentations, while doctoral students shared their work in a dedicated session, Tamkang faculty and students were able to exchange perspectives with futures scholars from a wide range of cultural and professional backgrounds. This also allowed them to reexamine their research within broader Asia-Pacific and global contexts. He noted that the university’s participation not only enhanced the international visibility of Tamkang’s futures studies research, but also demonstrated the results of its long-term commitment to cultivating talent in foresight thinking and interdisciplinary research, while continuing to deepen connections between Tamkang’s futures studies community and international academic networks.

title: Tamkang University's 15th Board of Trustees Takes Office, Flora Chia-I Chang Reappointed Chairperson with Unanimous Support 淡江大小事
heading: Date 2026-09-24 374 Clicks
text:
Date 2026-09-24 374 Clicks
The nine members of Tamkang University's 15th Board of Trustees were recently approved by the Ministry of Education (MOE), with their terms running from September 30, 2026, to September 29, 2030. In accordance with relevant regulations, the Board convened its first meeting on September 23. In the presence of certified public accountant Chih-Cheng Chou, a public-interest supervisor appointed by the MOE, all board members unanimously voted to reelect Flora Chia-I Chang, Chairperson of the 14th Board, to lead the 15th Board. The newly appointed Board will continue to fully support Tamkang University's institutional development and its ongoing pursuit of excellence as a model of sustainable higher education.
The nine members of the 15th Board of Trustees are Flora Chia-I Chang, Charles C. Lin, Hong-Shang Hong, Kun-Yen Lee, Sush-Der Lee, Yi-Pin Chien, Wu-Tien Chou, Shaw-Shing Wang, and Sun-Lu Fan, with Fan being the only newly appointed member. Fan holds a master's degree from Tamkang University's Graduate Institute of American Studies and was recognized as one of the university's 30th Golden Eagle Alumni Award recipients. She has held several prominent public offices, including Legislator, Deputy Minister of Education, Director-General of the Kaohsiung City Education Bureau, and Member of the Control Yuan. Her distinguished career has provided her with extensive experience in national legislation, public administration, and government oversight. Throughout her career, Fan has advanced educational innovation, adopting a forward-looking approach to formulating and implementing policies and legislation related to education, gender equality, and support for disadvantaged groups.
Chairperson Flora Chia-I Chang holds a doctorate in education from Stanford University and previously served as President of Tamkang University and Chairperson of the Foundation for International Cooperation in Higher Education of Taiwan (FICHET). During her presidency, she led Tamkang University to receive the 19th National Quality Award. Her individual achievements include the Excellence in Management Award at the 25th National Quality Awards, the 11th Individual Award from the Asia-Pacific Futures Network (APFN) in 2025, recognition as a Fellow of the Chinese Association for General Education in 2025, and the Individual Award for Promoting Quality Culture among Global Chinese Communities at the 11th Global Chinese Quality Summit in 2026.
During her tenure as Chairperson of the 13th and 14th Boards of Trustees, Chang strongly supported former President Huan-Chao Keh in advancing major institutional transformations, including dual-track development, digital transformation, and sustainability initiatives. Under the university's strategic visions represented by its two registered trademarks, "AI+SDGs=∞" and "ESG+AI=∞," Tamkang achieved the remarkable milestone of exceeding a 101% freshman enrollment rate in its full-time undergraduate programs for three consecutive years. At the inauguration ceremony of newly appointed President Hui-Huang Hsu, Chairperson Chang praised his extensive academic and administrative experience in Taiwan and internationally. She reaffirmed the Board's continued commitment to supporting the university's development and expressed her hope that Tamkang would usher in a new era of sustainable growth and excellence.
